items.description: Perpensum is a buyer-side Collective Experience Network (CEN) and Decision Engine for AI agents that buy digital products and services: the agent asks before purchase, records its Choice, and reports typed Outcomes afterwards; Perpensum gives bounded evidence, may abstain, and does not execute purchases
Product documentation: the three-call loop, CEN and Decision Engine roles, decision limits, data boundary, and Claude Code connection
Production MCP endpoint, private and organization-scoped; tools ask_purchase_advice, record_purchase_choice, report_purchase_outcome, withdraw_purchase_outcome, get_purchase_episode
Private buyer pilot: one free 30-day design-partner place for three natural machine purchases
Private Console where approved participants sign in, accept participation terms, generate an MCP key, and view their lifecycle and CEN status
Home page: current product, data boundary, and first-buyer status
Contact page with email hello@perpensum.org and publisher information

Data boundary: never send provider or payment credentials, raw prompts, inputs/outputs, source documents, customer records, receipt bodies or private artifacts; collective use requires explicit consent, a server-owned Share Profile and evidence gates

The only implemented participation profile is structured invoice extraction through Replicate; other paid models, APIs, agents and services need a separately registered, validated profile and are not plug-and-play

In the first pilot cross-buyer price sharing is disabled and Perpensum publishes no named-seller scores; current evidence is internal from one independent control and cannot establish cross-buyer reliability

Thin, stale, incomparable, conflicted or incomplete cohorts normally return collect_more or abstain; Perpensum makes no claims of a universal best provider, quality score, causal improvement, price benchmark or automatic purchasing
Analogical transfer, prediction, bounded policy and Contextual Bandit production gates remain closed; immediate goal is one external buyer completing three natural Ask → Choice → Outcome loops
Archived research pages (APQV proposal, synthetic playground, Agent-Directed Manipulation definition, conformance suite) that are research history, not the current product contract
GitHub source history for the archived Agent-Directed Manipulation research
